title: A split work order with one person on both sides prints one name
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Have an active staff member at the test location with the "Sales Representative" switch on: sales rep A.
  • Use a customer with no Sales Representative assigned.
  • Have an open, uninvoiced work order for that customer, with one approved labor line, one part and "Sales Representative - Labor" and "Sales Representative - Parts" both set to sales rep A.
  • Open the work order in a desktop browser at least 1024 pixels wide.
  • If you cannot set up any of the above, mark this test Blocked: "setup not done".
custom_steps:
1. Open the work order's menu.
  2. Click Print Work Order and read the Sales Representative row of the printout.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The work order's menu opens.

Step 2:

  • The printout opens.
  • The row reads sales rep A (one name).
  • It does not read "[sales rep A's name] (Parts) · [sales rep A's name] (Labor)".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Splitting Sales Representatives", Confluence 919928833, version 11 (21 Oct 2026, Chris Ward), read 22 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10890, story SV-11270 (Story 6, Print both representatives on the work order)

  • S6-R1: “The printed Sales Representative row reads the one name when one person holds both sides, for example "Devon Whitfield", or "Devon Whitfield (Inactive)" when they are inactive.”

From: Tech plan "Splitting Sales Representatives — Technical Implementation Plan" (dated 14 Oct 2026, planned against PRD version 8; uploaded 19 Oct 2026 and again, byte-identical, 22 Oct 2026), read in full 22 Oct 2026

  • Tech plan, print tests (Phase 5): “one person both sides (split or not) -> one name”
  • Tech plan, print and audit log (Phase 5): “Note the deliberate difference from print: a split entry reads both sides even when one person holds both (S7-R3 says "a split work order reads both sides"; S6-R1 collapses only on paper).”
